newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BEATEN AJAX COACH HAILS JUVENTUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BEATEN AJAX COACH HAILS JUVENTUS.

text.p: Ajax coach Louis van Gaal paid tribute to Juventus on Wednesday after the defending champions ripped apart his team 4-1 for a 6-2 aggregate to reach their second consecutive European Cup final.
"They are a great team with great skills. They are a pleasure to watch," said the coach, whose team were previously unbeaten away since the Champions' League started.
In the May 28 final in Munich Juventus now meet Germany's Borussia Dortmund, whose 2-1 win in Turin last season makes them the last club to have beaten the Italians in Europe.

The Turin team, on course to celebrate their 100th anniversary as Italian, European and World Club champions, demolished the Dutch in a strange match in which the visitors had by far the majority of possession.

Juventus, now into their fifth European Cup final in search of their third win, appeared determined to show what they were really made of after drawing 1-1 and then beating Ajax on penalties in last year's final in Rome.
But Juventus coach Marcello Lippi played such suggestions down in his usual deadpan style.
"We don't want to teach anyone any lessons," he said. "We just want to win."

Attilio Lombardo opened the scoring in the 34th minute with a header from a corner by French midfielder Zinedine Zidane and Christian Vieri then volleyed in at close range following a Lombardo cross to make it 2-0 in the 36th.
Both goals were completely against the run of play, with Ajax carving through a woeful Juventus defence in the opening 20 minutes but failing to find the net.
"They are a great team...but in the first half they were vulnerable and we did not take advantage," said Van Gaal.
Tijani Babangida could have put Ajax ahead after five minutes but his shot careered into the side-netting.
"We started a bit nervous, probably because of changes we had to make due to absences," Lippi said. "But after Lombardo scored and set up the second I saw a good Juve. Right to the end."
Ajax pulled a goal back in the 76th minute through Mario Melchiot but that seemed only to spur the champions to greater efforts -- with Zidane at the heart of things.
In the 80th minute he set-up Nicola Amoruso after doing all the hard work and then passing for a simple tap-in.

Two minutes later he scored a virtuoso goal as the fans chanted his name and that of Lippi, who has now taken Juventus to three consecutive European finals. In 1995 they lost the UEFA Cup final to Parma.
"Zidane is very dangerous whenever there is space. When we had to attack and made space, he took advantage of it," said Van Gaal.

Lippi said he did not think the fact that the final would be played in Germany would have much bearing on the outcome. "Half the stadium will be behind us," he said. "We are the favourites but we will not be influenced by that."

Only Internazionale, who reached the UEFA Cup final on Tuesday by beating Monaco, have previously won the Italian league title, the European Cup and the World Club Cup in the same season. They achieved the feat in 1964-65.
Juventus are already the World Club champions and have a six-point lead at the top of serie A.
